meta.purpose: Human rubric calibration for technical_demand and load_demand (1-4). Both fields are intentionally empty and must be filled in by a person.
meta.full_library_sheet: data/review/demand-library.v1.csv — same columns, all 239 eligible primaries. Grades entered here transfer by template_id.

technical_demand.means: How much skill this session assumes.
technical_demand.consequence: Matched as a HARD constraint once set — technical demand above an athlete's capacity makes the session ineligible, not merely disfavoured. Grading one point too high silently removes a session from a library that is already thin in some domains; one point too low is a safety question.

load_demand.means: How much this session costs to absorb: volume, intensity, recovery required.
load_demand.consequence: Read when the planner filters the candidate pool.

grading_fields.null_semantics: Empty = ungraded. Every matching rule reads null as "do not constrain", so an ungraded template behaves exactly as it does today.

columns.note: Columns prefixed ref_ are flattened from workout_blocks, block_exercises and workout_variants for reading. Edits to them cannot be imported — changing a prescription means editing a content pack and going through scripts/prepare-pack.mjs and scripts/import-workouts.mjs, which enforce the explicit-unit rule and semantic dedup that this sheet does not.

sampling_frame.stresses: Absolute floor: lowest intensity, one movement, no structure. Anchors 1/1.
Recovery that is still multi-modal — does "recovery" force technical_demand to 1?
Joint-shortest session (10 min), single station. Floor of the duration axis.
Intermediate movement at RPE 7-8 prescribed in "steps" — a unit with no load or time in it.
Short (18 min) but high-impact and intermediate-complexity. Duration pulls down, everything else pulls up.
Longest threshold session, three blocks, duration and distance prescribed in the same workout.
RPE band spans 6-8 within one session — which end does a single load grade take?
Strength stripped to 15 minutes. Tests whether session_type=strength carries a demand floor.
Forty minutes of maintenance strength at RPE 5-6 — long but deliberately undemanding.
Advanced-complexity movement, four modalities, and rep RANGES (x10-12) rather than fixed reps.
Advanced complexity plus an open-ended AMRAP-2 item — prescribed work with no fixed quantity.
Twelve easy minutes, one movement. The easy anchor for a non-recovery domain.
DECOUPLING CASE: RPE 3-4 and 15 minutes, but high impact and intermediate complexity. Low load, high technique.
DECOUPLING CASE: longest session in the library (75 min) at RPE 3-4 on one movement. High load, no technique.
Six blocks — most structurally segmented session in the library — on a single trivial movement.
DECOUPLING CASE: ten minutes at RPE 8-9. Shortest possible session, highest prescribed intensity.
Twenty minutes across four blocks at RPE 3-6 — taper work that looks busier than it is.
Five exercises across four modalities in twenty minutes, on an EMOM clock.
Race simulation: 75 min, high impact, RPE 7. The intended ceiling of load.
Structural ceiling: six blocks, seven exercises, four modalities, 75 minutes.

caveats: block_exercises.load_basis and .load_value are unpopulated across all 765 rows in the seed, so no absolute external load is available anywhere in the library. Load grading rests on prescribed volume, RPE and movement.
Four primary templates carry status=retired and were excluded from the sampling population.
